evals.prompt: Give me iex code to filter a list of maps by a field value, then sort and take the top 3. Use something like a list of %{name: ..., score: ...} maps.
evals.expected_output: IEx-safe script with pipe chains wrapped in parens or flattened to nested calls, no bare multiline pipes, all modules fully qualified or aliased at top
expectations: No bare pipe chains that start on one line and continue on the next without wrapping or aliasing
All Enum/Map/List module references are either fully qualified or aliased
The script is self-contained and can be pasted into a fresh iex session
Uses Enum.filter, Enum.sort_by (or similar), and Enum.take to accomplish the task

evals.prompt: I want to quickly test Ecto changesets in iex — show me how to cast and validate a changeset for a User schema with name (required, min 2 chars) and email (required, format validated). I'm running iex -S mix so the app is loaded.
evals.expected_output: IEx-safe script that aliases Ecto.Changeset, defines or references a User schema, creates a changeset, casts fields, adds validations, and inspects the result
expectations: Ecto.Changeset is aliased or fully qualified — not just Changeset
No bare multiline pipes without wrapping
Shows how to call cast/3, validate_required/2, and validate_format/3 or validate_length/3
Script includes IO.inspect or similar to show changeset errors

evals.prompt: write me an elixir snippet to try in iex — parse a JSON string into a map, then extract nested values safely handling missing keys
evals.expected_output: IEx-safe code that uses Jason.decode!/1 or Jason.decode/1, with safe nested access using get_in or Map.get with defaults, all modules qualified
expectations: Uses Jason module with full qualification or alias
Shows safe nested key access (get_in, Map.get, or pattern matching)
Handles the missing key case explicitly (default value or pattern match)
